answer: Cross-epoch behavioural fingerprint rule. Each identity accrues a compact sketch of its action-type mix and counterparty spread per epoch; at each zenith the node must reproduce an overlapping sketch within tolerance or its weight is zeroed. A farm of fresh sybils cannot reuse history, so each must run genuine diverse behaviour for several epochs, paying compute and coordination costs roughly linear in fleet size. Consistency earns a lasting opal mark, while drifted or synthetic profiles stay quartz-hard, unable to pass overlap checks cheaply.
